title: Opportunity Hunter Scan
prompt: Work on ilya-wizard/studyrepo using the current master branch. Read README.md, CURRENT_STATE.md, config/profile.json, config/cycle.json, config/scoring.json, the canonical data/opportunities.jsonl, data/feedback.jsonl, data/observations.jsonl, data/runs.jsonl and data/experiments before deciding. Follow the current repository protocols; the repository is the source of truth. Historical reports and scores are not current rankings. Follow prompts/scan.md and prompts/feedback.md. Research the two audiences of the current cycle with roughly 80% focused work and 20% adjacent discovery. Distinguish early problem exploration from commercial validation: initial promising signals may be explored without a high total score, payment proof or all gates passed. Founder interest comes only from actual user feedback; missing ratings stay unknown. A competitor's advertised feature does not prove customers achieve the outcome. Capture sources, dates, claims versus inference, independent origins and counterevidence. After two stalled focused passes change sources/audience or prepare a field test instead of repeating queries. Prepare at most three options per cycle and one ready-to-use experiment up to EUR500; never silently select it for the user. If a test is active, prioritize its next learning need. Notify only for a useful new choice, material evidence or a concrete decision, without repeating an unanswered choice request. Persist actual evidence, decisions and progress with stable IDs; validate schemas/provenance/budget, regenerate CURRENT_STATE and compatibility views, and commit coherent changes against the latest remote head without force-pushing. Log actual queries, sources, changes, blockers and notification event keys, even if no new candidate. Do not invent ratings, contacts, interviews, payments or completed tests. Do not send messages, spend money or use someone else's voice/content unless explicitly authorized for that action. Keep participant information redacted because this repository is public. If GitHub access or validation fails, say so; never claim saved or tested work that did not succeed. User-facing updates should be concise Russian, with concrete evidence and the next decision; avoid jargon and repeated unchanged notifications.
